blogs.title: The Pulmonary Mask of Pancreatitis: When Recurrent Pleural Effusions Aren’t a Chest Problem
blogs.description: This post would explore pancreatopleural fistula as a classic extrathoracic cause of recurrent massive pleural effusion, especially in children presenting primarily with dyspnoea and chest pain rather than abdominal symptoms. It would focus on the diagnostic pitfall of anchoring on pulmonary or pleural disease while the real pathology lies in the pancreas, and discuss when clinicians should broaden the differential after repeat thoracenteses and rapid reaccumulation.

blogs.title: Hemorrhagic Pleural Effusion in a Child: Don’t Forget to Ask About Trauma
blogs.description: This post would use the delayed disclosure of bicycle-handle abdominal trauma to highlight the importance of repeated, high-quality history-taking when the clinical course doesn’t fit the initial diagnosis. It would discuss how blunt pancreatic trauma can present weeks later with respiratory symptoms, why children may minimize or hide trauma history, and how that history can radically redirect evaluation away from tuberculosis, infection, or malignancy.

blogs.title: Pleural Fluid Amylase: The Underused Test That Can End a Diagnostic Odyssey
blogs.description: This post would focus on the role of pleural fluid amylase and lipase in evaluating recurrent exudative or blood-stained effusions. It would review the differential diagnosis of amylase-rich pleural fluid—pancreatopleural fistula, oesophageal perforation, and malignancy—while emphasizing that very high levels should trigger urgent pancreatic imaging and consideration of amylase isoenzyme testing to distinguish pancreatic from salivary sources.

blogs.title: CT, MRCP, or ERCP? Imaging Strategy for Suspected Pancreatopleural Fistula
blogs.description: This post would analyze the strengths and limitations of different imaging modalities in suspected pancreatopleural fistula. It would compare CT for identifying associated collections and thoracic complications, MRCP for noninvasive delineation of ductal anatomy and fistulous tracts, and ERCP as both a diagnostic and therapeutic tool, offering a practical stepwise imaging approach for clinicians facing recurrent unexplained pleural effusions.

blogs.title: Conservative First, but Not Forever: Managing Pancreatopleural Fistula in Children
blogs.description: This post would examine the management tension between initial medical therapy and early escalation to endoscopic or surgical intervention. Using this child’s successful course with chest drainage, bowel rest, TPN, octreotide, and pancreatic enzyme replacement, it would review what conservative care is trying to achieve, how long to persist, which ductal features predict failure, and when ERCP-guided stenting or surgery should move to the front of the plan.

blogs.title: TB, ADA, and Anchoring Bias: Lessons from a Recurrent Effusion That Wasn’t Tuberculosis
blogs.description: This post would discuss the cognitive errors that arise in high-prevalence settings when mild ADA elevation and TB contact history drive empiric antitubercular treatment. It would use the case to teach a more nuanced approach to pleural ADA interpretation, highlight the dangers of premature closure in recurrent hemorrhagic effusions, and offer strategies for reassessing the diagnosis when the patient keeps returning with the same problem.
